image_description: A grey whale tail fluke emerging vertically from the ocean surface, displaying a dark grey to black coloration with mottled white patches and barnacle encrustations. The fluke shows a smooth trailing edge with a distinct central notch. The surrounding water is blue-grey with gentle ripples and foam at the base of the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is completely submerged and not visible in the frame; only the tail fluke is shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible on the tail fluke surface: clear mottling pattern with lighter grey/white patches consistent with barnacle encrustations typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal region/knuckles are not visible as only the tail fluke emerges from water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the tail fluke is visible; the main body remains submerged and cannot be assessed for shape or proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Clearly visible on the fluke surface - characteristic grey whale skin texture with barnacle-induced light patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Baleen plates are internal mouth structures not visible when the whale is diving with only tail exposed.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are submerged and not visible in this tail-fluke-only view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Perfectly matches: the fluke is broad, has a smooth trailing edge without raggedness, and displays a clear central notch/divot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Surface texture appears appropriately rough with visible raised areas consistent with callosities/barnacles on grey whale skin.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the very edges of the fluke where it meets the sky background, possibly indicating minor edge bleeding or AI generation smoothing, but within acceptable range for photographic realism.

The foam/water disturbance at the base of the fluke appears slightly uniform and lacks the chaotic detail expected from a massive whale's movement, suggesting possible simplification in water physics simulation.
